title: Wildlife Tourism in Kerala: Periyar, Wayanad, Thattekad and More

metaDescription: Plan a wildlife trip in Kerala: Periyar's boat trips and walks, Wayanad, Parambikulam, Eravikulam's Nilgiri tahr, Thattekad's birds, Chinnar and Silent Valley.
description: A guide to wildlife tourism in Kerala: Periyar Tiger Reserve at Thekkady with boat trips and guided walks, Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary, Parambikulam Tiger Reserve, Eravikulam National Park and the Nilgiri tahr, Silent Valley, Chinnar, Thattekad Bird Sanctuary and Kumarakom, with seasons, community-run programmes and routes.
dek: Kerala's wildlife lives in the forests of the Western Ghats, one of the world's biodiversity hotspots. Here is where to go and what to expect.

hero.alt: A safari jeep on a forest track in Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary

intro: Kerala's protected areas run along the Western Ghats, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its biodiversity. The state has two tiger reserves, Periyar and Parambikulam, and national parks including Eravikulam and Silent Valley.

Wildlife viewing in Kerala is different from central India. Forests are dense and wet, so sightings are less frequent, but the state has pioneered community-run programmes, such as guided walks and bamboo rafting at Periyar, run with former forest-dependent communities.
quickAnswer: Kerala's main wildlife destinations are Periyar Tiger Reserve at Thekkady, known for boat trips on Periyar lake and guided nature walks; Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary for elephants and jeep safaris; Parambikulam Tiger Reserve; Eravikulam National Park near Munnar for the Nilgiri tahr; and Thattekad for birds. October to May is the main season, though Eravikulam closes for tahr calving in roughly February and March.
takeaways: Periyar is best known for boat trips and community-run walks and bamboo rafting.
Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary runs jeep safaris from Muthanga and Tholpetty.
Eravikulam near Munnar protects the Nilgiri tahr and closes for calving, roughly February to March.
Thattekad is one of south India's best birding sites.
Dense forests mean fewer sightings than central India; enjoy the forest itself.

items.name: Periyar
body: Boat trips on the lake formed by the Mullaperiyar dam, with elephants, gaur and sambar on the banks, plus walks, bamboo rafting and border hiking run by the forest department with local communities.

image.caption: Periyar lake, Thekkady

items.name: Wayanad
body: Jeep safaris in the Muthanga and Tholpetty ranges, part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

items.name: Eravikulam
body: A forest department bus takes visitors to the Rajamala area, where Nilgiri tahr graze on rolling grassland.

items.name: Parambikulam
body: A tiger reserve with teak forest and reservoirs, known for community-run tourism packages.

sections.heading: Community-run programmes
paras: Periyar pioneered eco-development in Indian tiger reserves. Former poachers and forest-dependent villagers were trained as guides and now run treks, bamboo rafting and night patrols with the forest department. Booking these activities directly supports their work.
Parambikulam follows a similar model, with packages run by local eco-development committees that include tented stays, treks and bamboo rafts.

sections.heading: Tips for wildlife in Kerala
list: Book Periyar's walks and bamboo rafting in advance; group sizes are small and slots fill up.
Take the first boat of the day on Periyar lake, when animals are more likely at the water.
Go with a local bird guide at Thattekad; many forest birds are shy and hard to find.
Allow for slow hill roads between Munnar, Thekkady and Wayanad.

rows: Pleasant; good for walks and birds
Warmer; animals near water in Periyar and Wayanad
Heavy monsoon; some activities suspended; forests at their greenest

sections.heading: Where to stay and how long
paras: Thekkady has hotels and homestays in Kumily town and forest department stays inside Periyar. Wayanad has resorts and homestays among coffee estates. Munnar suits Eravikulam and Chinnar. Two nights at each place is enough; a week can cover Munnar, Thekkady and the backwaters.

rows: Kochi to Thattekad for birds, then Munnar
Thekkady: boat trip, guided walk, bamboo rafting

safety: Sightings are never guaranteed; plan several drives and enjoy the forest itself.
Stay in the vehicle on safaris and follow your guide.
Book permits only through official forest department portals or trusted operators.
Never feed animals or leave litter in a park.
Leeches are common in the wet season; wear leech socks on walks.

faqs.q: Which is the best wildlife sanctuary in Kerala?
faqs.a: Periyar Tiger Reserve at Thekkady is the most visited; Wayanad and Parambikulam are good for mammals.

faqs.q: Can you see tigers in Periyar?
faqs.a: Tigers live in Periyar but are rarely seen; elephants, gaur and sambar are more common.

faqs.q: Is Kerala good for a wildlife holiday with children?
faqs.a: Yes. Boat trips at Periyar, the bus ride at Eravikulam and jeep safaris in Wayanad all suit families.
